tutorial_example_entry.lesson_core_move: Classify unstable continuous-time systems by applying the BIBO criterion to recognize bounded inputs that produce unbounded output growth due to insufficient damping or reinforcing dynamics.

blocks.text: A continuous-time system is unstable when it fails the bounded-input bounded-output criterion: there exists a bounded input that produces an output with no finite bound. The cue is simple - if the input stays bounded but the output can still grow without limit, the system is unstable.

A bounded input stays inside some finite ceiling $M$, and a bounded output would stay inside some finite ceiling $N$. Instability appears when you can name a bounded input but cannot find any finite bound on the corresponding output.

Start with the simplest failure case: $x(t)=\sin t$ is bounded, but $y(t)=t\sin t$ is not, because its envelope grows like $|t|$. The input remains under control while the output grows without bound, so the system is unstable.

The growth can come from insufficient damping or from reinforcing dynamics, but the first test is always the same: decide whether the output stays bounded for bounded input. Later examples will separate true divergence from merely large but finite behavior.
Keep the classification rule fixed: bounded input plus unbounded output means instability. That is the definition the next examples will keep reusing.

example_content.example_prompt: A bounded input $x(t)=\sin t$ produces output $y(t)=t\sin t$. Decide whether the output is bounded or unbounded and state what that means for the system.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is the bounded input: $x(t)=\sin t$ stays between $-1$ and $1$, so it is bounded.
Now inspect the output $y(t)=t\sin t$. The sinusoid still oscillates, but the factor $t$ makes the envelope grow without bound as $t$ increases.
Because no finite $N$ can bound $|y(t)|$ for all $t$, the output is unbounded. A bounded input has produced an unbounded output, so the system fails BIBO stability and is unstable.

sections.section_title: Distinguishing Large Bounded Outputs from Unbounded Outputs

example_content.example_prompt: A bounded input $x(t)=\cos t$ produces output $y(t)=10\sin t$. Decide whether the output is merely large or actually unbounded.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is still a bounded input: $x(t)=\cos t$ stays between $-1$ and $1$, so the input is bounded.
Now inspect the output $y(t)=10\sin t$. The amplitude is large, but the factor $10$ is fixed, so the envelope does not grow with $t$.

Because the output stays within a finite bound, it is bounded rather than unbounded. This behavior does not make the system unstable, because size alone is not the BIBO test; the envelope must grow without bound to fail stability.

example_content.example_prompt: A bounded input $x(t)=\sin t$ produces output $y(t)=e^{0.2t}\sin t$. Decide whether the system is unstable and explain why the damping interpretation matters.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is the bounded input: $x(t)=\sin t$ stays between $-1$ and $1$, so the input is bounded.

Now inspect the output $y(t)=e^{0.2t}\sin t$. The sine term still oscillates, but the envelope is $e^{0.2t}$, and that factor grows with $t$ instead of decaying. That is the sign of insufficient damping.

Because the envelope keeps increasing, no finite $N$ can bound $|y(t)|$ for all $t$. The response is unbounded, so a bounded input has produced an unbounded output and the system fails BIBO stability.

example_content.example_prompt: A bounded input $x(t)=u(t)$ passes through a system with output $y(t)=\int_0^t x(\tau)\,d\tau$. Decide whether the output stays bounded or grows without bound.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is the bounded input $x(t)=u(t)$. It stays at $0$ or $1$, so the input is bounded.
The output is an accumulated response, $y(t)=\int_0^t x(\tau)\,d\tau$. For this input, the system keeps adding positive area, so the response grows instead of settling.

Substituting the bounded input gives $y(t)=\int_0^t 1\,d\tau=t$ for $t\ge 0$, or equivalently $y(t)=t\,u(t)$. That is a ramp with no finite upper bound, so the output is unbounded because of reinforcing dynamics.

Since a bounded input produced an unbounded output, the system fails BIBO stability and is unstable. The cause here is reinforcing accumulation: each new bit of input adds more output instead of being damped away.

sections.section_title: Classifying an Unstable System from Input-Output Behavior

example_content.example_prompt: A bounded input produces $y(t)=t\cos t + 3\sin t$. Classify the system and name the term that makes the output unbounded.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is the mixed response $y(t)=t\cos t + 3\sin t$ coming from a bounded input. The question is not whether part of the output is bounded; it is whether the full output has a finite bound.
Split the response into two terms. The $3\sin t$ term is bounded, but the $t\cos t$ term has an envelope that grows like $|t|$, so it has no finite upper bound.
Because the unbounded term dominates the bounded add-on, the whole output is unbounded. A bounded input has produced an unbounded output, so the system is unstable by the BIBO criterion.

question_entry.lesson_core_move: Classify unstable continuous-time systems by applying the BIBO criterion to recognize bounded inputs that produce unbounded output growth due to insufficient damping or reinforcing dynamics.

prompt_blocks.text: For bounded input $x(t)=\cos t$, the system rule gives $y(t)=t\cos t$. Decide whether the output is bounded and what this implies for BIBO stability.

choice_blocks.text: Output is bounded because sine/cosine terms are bounded and their product always stays finite.
Output is bounded since $x(t)$ is bounded and multiplying by time cannot create unbounded output in this setting.
Output is unbounded because $|y(t)|=|t||\cos t|$ has an envelope that grows without bound, so a bounded input produced an unbounded output and the system is unstable.
The answer depends on whether $t$ is positive, so no single classification can be made without plotting sample points.
Because the signal oscillates, the system must be stable even when multiplied by $t$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: $x(t)=\cos t$ is bounded because $|\cos t|\le1$ for all $t$, but $|y(t)|=|t||\cos t|$ grows without a finite upper bound as $|t|\to\infty$. One bounded input creating an unbounded output violates BIBO stability.

prompt_blocks.text: Given bounded input $x(t)=\sin t$, decide the boundedness of $y(t)=e^t x(t)$ and the stability verdict for this system rule.

choice_blocks.text: Stable, because $|\sin t|\le1$ and periodic inputs always yield bounded outputs.
Unstable: $|y(t)|=e^t|\sin t|$ becomes arbitrarily large, so a bounded input produced unbounded output growth.
Unstable only for very negative time, where the exponential term decays and then reverses growth.
Undetermined from the expression, since both input and output must be plotted over many periods.
Stable, because the input is bounded and the bounded-input/outcome examples in this topic all use algebraic gains only.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The input is bounded since $|\sin t|\le1$, but $|y(t)|=e^t|\sin t|$. As $t\to\infty$, the factor $e^t$ diverges, so no finite bound on $|y(t)|$ exists. This is a bounded-input, unbounded-output counterexample, so the system is not BIBO stable.

sections.section_title: Distinguishing Large Bounded Outputs from Unbounded Outputs

prompt_blocks.text: A bounded input $x(t)=\cos t$ produces $y(t)=12\sin t$. Decide whether the output is merely large or actually unbounded.

choice_blocks.text: The output is bounded because the amplitude is fixed and $|y(t)|\le 12$ for all $t$.
The output is unbounded because it is very large in magnitude even though it oscillates.
The output is unbounded because every sine output grows without limit in time.
The output is unbounded unless $x(t)$ has zero mean and finite energy.
There is not enough information because $\sin t$ is not explicitly bounded in the interval shown.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: $x(t)=\cos t$ is bounded, and the output has fixed envelope $12$. Since $|\sin t|\le 1$, the magnitude is $|y(t)|=|12\sin t|\le 12$, so it is bounded for all $t$.

prompt_blocks.text: A bounded input $x(t)=\sin t$ produces $y(t)=10e^{0.4t}\sin t$. Choose the correct classification.

choice_blocks.text: The output is unbounded because $e^{0.4t}$ causes growth that is not capped by a fixed envelope.
The output is bounded because $\sin t$ itself is bounded between $-1$ and $1$.
The output is bounded because the coefficient $10$ is fixed, so exponential terms cannot increase magnitude.
The output is bounded if the input is zero at $t=0$ but unbounded otherwise.
The output is bounded because bounded-input tests require checking only $t\ge 0$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: $\sin t$ is bounded, but $e^{0.4t}$ is not. The output magnitude is $|y(t)|=10e^{0.4t}|\sin t|$, and because $e^{0.4t}$ grows without bound as $t\to\infty$, the output has no finite uniform bound.

prompt_blocks.text: A bounded input $x(t)=\cos(2t)$ produces $y(t)=e^{0.1t}\cos(2t)$. Classify the response and state whether the system is BIBO stable.

choice_blocks.text: Stable, because sinusoidal terms are bounded and cannot produce unbounded outputs.
Stable, because the exponential factor decays from $0$ to $1$ over time.
Unstable, because the bounded input is multiplied by $e^{0.1t}$, whose envelope grows with $t$.
Unstable only at isolated points where $\cos(2t)=0$.
Cannot classify because the input magnitude is missing from the prompt.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: $x(t)=\cos(2t)$ is bounded, but $|y(t)|=e^{0.1t}|\cos(2t)|$. The exponential envelope grows without bound, so there is no finite bound for the output.

prompt_blocks.text: For bounded input $x(t)=5\cos(3t-\pi/4)$, the output is $y(t)=\frac{1}{2}e^{0.25t}\cos(3t-\pi/4)$. What is the correct stability conclusion?

choice_blocks.text: Stable, because a sinusoidal input means the output is always bounded.
Stable, because $\frac{1}{2}$ is a small coefficient and therefore enforces decay.
Unstable, because the envelope is $\frac{1}{2}e^{0.25t}$, which grows over time.
Unstable only for negative time because of the negative phase shift.
Stable, because the input is bounded and there is no additive forcing term.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The input is bounded, but $|y(t)|=\frac{1}{2}e^{0.25t}|\cos(3t-\pi/4)|$. The exponential envelope increases without bound, so a bounded input does not imply bounded output.

prompt_blocks.text: A bounded input $x(t)=2u(t-2)$ drives the system $y(t)=\int_0^t x(\tau)\,d\tau$. Decide whether this input-output pair is BIBO-stable for this step.

choice_blocks.text: The input is bounded, but the response accumulates to a shifted ramp. For $t\ge 2$, $y(t)=\int_2^t 2\,d\tau=2(t-2)$, which is unbounded, so the system is unstable due to reinforcing accumulation.
Because integration smooths the input, any bounded input is guaranteed to remain bounded at the output.
Since $|x(t)|\le 2$, the output is bounded by $|y(t)|\le 2$ for all $t$.
This is stable, because the integral sign means you can ignore the ramp shape and only track the bounded range of $x(t)$.
The output is directly bounded by the constant $2u(t-2)$ term, so it can never exceed that value.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The input $x(t)=2u(t-2)$ is bounded, so the BIBO check applies. Substitute into the rule for the system: $y(t)=\int_0^t 2u(\tau-2)\,d\tau$. For $t<2$, $y(t)=0$; for $t\ge2$, $y(t)=\int_2^t 2\,d\tau=2(t-2)$, which has no finite upper bound. A bounded input with unbounded output means the system is unstable.

prompt_blocks.text: Test the pair $y(t)=\int_0^t x(\tau)\,d\tau$ with bounded input $x(t)=1+0.5\sin t$. What is the correct conclusion?

choice_blocks.text: Input is bounded, but output keeps accumulating net positive area. Since $y(t)=\int_0^t (1+0.5\sin\tau)\,d\tau=t-0.5\cos t+0.5\sin 0$, it grows without bound, so the system is unstable due to reinforcing dynamics.
Since $|x(t)|\le 1.5$, a bound $|y(t)|\le 1.5$ exists, so the system is BIBO stable.
The bounded sine term in $x(t)$ keeps the integral bounded by cancellation, so the system is stable no matter what is added to it.
Do not use the step model here; because there is an oscillatory component, the output is $y(t)=\sin t$, which is bounded.
A bounded input cannot create unbounded output for an integrator rule because integration is always damping-like.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The input is bounded because $1+0.5\sin t$ stays between $0.5$ and $1.5$. Substituting into the system integral gives $y(t)=\int_0^t 1\,d\tau+0.5\int_0^t\sin \tau\,d\tau=t+0.5(1-\cos t)=t-0.5\cos t+0.5$. The linear term $t$ dominates and makes $|y(t)|$ unbounded, so BIBO stability fails.

sections.section_title: Classifying an Unstable System from Input-Output Behavior

prompt_blocks.text: A bounded input produces $y(t)=2t\sin t-4\cos t$. Classify the system and name the term that makes the output unbounded.

choice_blocks.text: Unstable: the $2t\sin t$ term is unbounded, so the full output is unbounded.
Stable: the output is bounded because $\sin t$ and $\cos t$ are bounded.
Unstable because $-4\cos t$ dominates and can grow without bound.
Stable, since the unbounded-looking term is multiplied by a bounded sine.
Unstable because the bounded add-on $-4\cos t$ alone makes BIBO fail.

questions.correct_answer: The system is unstable because $2t\sin t$ is unbounded.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Split the output into $2t\sin t$ and $-4\cos t$. The $-4\cos t$ term is bounded, but $|2t\sin t|$ has an envelope that grows like $2|t|$, so $\sup_t |y(t)|=\infty$. A bounded input produced an unbounded output, so the system is unstable by BIBO.

prompt_blocks.text: A bounded input produces $y(t)=t\cos(2t)+5\sin t+1$. Classify the system and identify the term that controls this result.

choice_blocks.text: Unstable, because $t\cos(2t)$ grows in envelope and makes $y(t)$ unbounded.
Stable, because both trigonometric terms are bounded and the $+1$ shift does not change stability.
Stable, because the input is bounded and all terms are bounded in form.
Unstable, because $5\sin t$ creates unbounded growth over time.
Unstable, but only because $1$ is the unbounded baseline term.

questions.correct_answer: The system is unstable because the $t\cos(2t)$ component is unbounded.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The constant $5\sin t+1$ block is bounded, so it cannot force unboundedness. The envelope of $t\cos(2t)$ scales like $|t|$, so no finite global bound exists for $|y(t)|$ and the system is unstable under BIBO.
